items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: Joe was very good. I played with him a lot too.

ctx.x: Well, Joe was good too. Joe was very good. I played with him a lot too. Well, Joe was powerful. He didn't have too much of a tone, but he was good for jazz because he could make all that, he could make it go like a dog and all that, you understand? You know, that wah-wah stuff and he'd make all that on the horn, you know? And he was strong, you know, he's a big fella, as big as you, you know? You saw him, huh? No. You ever seen? Same picture, he's a terrible picture. Yeah, he was a very big fella. I got a picture…
Not as big as me, though.

items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: So he played with us, you know, and made it all right with tunes that he knew, you know.

ctx.x: He played a sweeter tone than Bradley, I guess, did he?

Well, he had a little bit of tone, yeah, because he was taught, you know. He was a good teacher, you know. After he knew the fundamentals, you know, up to the horn, you know. Do you remember Joe Oliver? Well Joe come up, just like those other fellas, you know, starting out like that. I remember when I first saw him, I was playing with that Eagle band then. And we was playing on Rampart Street one night, just the trombones and the violin and the guitar and bass. So he came in this place with his horn, you know,…
Do you remember much about Freda Cuppert? I remember about Freda.
